_about: Where data that came from an online source goes (docs/44 'Data: nothing duplicated, lost or looped', the table's
Nightscout row): per origin, per target, 'yes' (sent as from any first-hand source), 'no' (never: back to where it
came from, or a service with one uploader per account), 'off' (off unless the person turns it on, a switch that says
why) or 'unlabelled' (sent without a sensor label, rule 7: no loop trusts internet readings as a sensor's). Rows:
'nightscout' = glucose read from the source site; 'nightscout-treatments' = treatments pulled from it (read-only
here). Targets: libreView (the LibreView upload), tidepool (the Tidepool upload), nightscoutSame (Nightscout upload
to the source's own site: the upload pauses while that site is the source, its treatments go both ways through the
source), nightscoutOther (upload to another site), healthConnect, followers (Sukrara's own sharing, your glucose
only), broadcasts (apps on the phone, Garmin). Someone else's glucose is never shared or uploaded whatever its source
(sources.json keying 'owner'); a Mac on its own uploads nothing. The treatments Sukrara logs itself keep today's
rules, plus both ways with the source site.
